paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage is really about: Jesus tells the truth about who He is, and He does it when it costs Him everything. The council can't get their witnesses to agree, and Jesus stays silent through all of it. But when the high priest asks, "Are You the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?" He says, "I am" (Mark 14:61-62). Right there He could have said nothing and walked out, and He chose to say who He is anyway.

Now look at Peter, because I think he's the baker's mirror. He followed Jesus right into that courtyard, and three questions later he's saying, "I do not know this man of whom you speak!" (Mark 14:71). Friend, I've been in a junk drawer long enough to know how big a fall feels when you landed it yourself. Here's the lesson: loving Jesus and failing Him can happen on the very same night, and the rooster doesn't care how loud you promised.

But hold on, because Peter's tears matter. He remembers the word Jesus spoke to him, and he breaks down and weeps (Mark 14:72). Jesus knew what Peter would do and said it ahead of time, and the words He spoke are what brought Peter back to himself. So when you stumble, baker, go back to what Jesus has said. And stay close, because this story is NOT over.
